notes: What is blinded: in TreeMcts::expand, when the node's player to move is not the searching seat, legal moves are generated on the real world state; then the whole evaluation part (battle-box / dialog-box folds, priors, leaf value incl. window resolution and leaf rollout) runs on a fresh Session over determinize_self_with(real, me) — my hand + deck + face-down life reshuffled as one pool, opponent side and public zones untouched, zone sizes and face-up life kept. The chosen fold index / priors apply to the real legal list; descent and move application stay on the real world (test (c) checks the real state is unchanged after expansion).

Board RNG (CRN): the session's game RNG is lent to the blinded copy and restored to its pre-evaluation snapshot afterwards (each evaluation path already restored it in the default code, so consumption order is unchanged).

Blind RNG: a separate Pcg32 per tree, seeded with (search_seed + world index) XOR 0x0B11D5EED0FF5EED, so it never touches the world-sampling/Dirichlet stream; deterministic per world and per thread. Paths without search_seed (recorded-RNG oracle) use the constant with seed 0 (still deterministic).

Item 4 (boxes where the opponent chooses): the in-tree battle/dialog box folds at opponent nodes are computed on the blinded copy. NOT blinded: opponent choices made inside window resolution that starts from MY nodes (resolve_battle_inplace's quiesce_choice priors and nested box picks during my leaf values / my box folds), the root window fold (window_choice) and the commit paths (dialog/setup box) — those are my own decisions evaluated in the sampled world. Threading the blind context into quiesce would be needed to cover them.

Inside an opponent node's evaluation, the window resolution also plays MY replies in the blinded world (i.e. the opponent's model of me). This is the 'opponent's view' evaluation as a whole, not only the net call.
Cards of mine that were publicly revealed earlier (e.g. by effects) are not tracked; everything in my hand is treated as hidden from the opponent.
If an opponent move in a box fold references one of my hidden cards by uuid, applying it on the blinded copy may fail; that branch then counts as None (same as any failing branch).

Combinations: works with worlds>1 (each world thread has its own blind RNG), reveal (opp_hand/fair: the world is sampled first, then my side is reshuffled again at opponent nodes), omniscient (opponent side real; meaning 'only the opponent is fair'). Test (d) covers all.

Default (opp_blind=false): TreeMcts.opp_blind is None and expand goes straight to the original code path (expand_eval with the real session); test (a) checks decide output and RNG consumption are bit-identical; audit-cross default wr equals rs-reveal's.
